# Vendored FreeType 2.6.3

The FreeType the DeBeOS image's `app_server` rasterises its glyphs with,
configured the way that image's package was built, so the client's text is the
server's text pixel for pixel. Every build of the client uses it unless it is
built with `HAIKU_REMOTE_FREETYPE=system` (Makefile) or
`-DHAIKU_REMOTE_FREETYPE=SYSTEM` (CMake), whose text then differs.

## What is here

Unmodified files from that tarball: `include/`, and the `.c`/`.h` files of the
modules the image's library has -- `src/base` and `autofit bdf cff cid gzip
lzw pcf pfr psaux pshinter psnames raster sfnt smooth truetype type1 type42
winfonts`. Left out: FreeType's own build systems, docs and tests, and the
modules that are not compiled into the image's library or not used here
(`bzip2`, which the recipe disables; `cache`, `gxvalid`, `otvalid`, `tools`).
`sources.txt` lists the translation units, one per module as FreeType's own
build compiles them; the Makefile, CMakeLists.txt and the painter oracle all
read it.

Not from the tarball:

- `haiku-config/freetype/config/ftmodule.h` is the module list the package's
  configure generated, copied from its installed headers. It is searched ahead
  of the stock `include/freetype/config/ftmodule.h`, which lists the same
  modules in another order; the order is the order FreeType tries drivers in
  when it opens a file, so it is the package's that is used.
- `haiku-config/apple-zlib-byte.h` is force-included into `src/gzip/ftgzip.c`
  on Apple targets only: the zlib 1.1.4 inside 2.6.3 skips its `Byte` typedef
  whenever `TARGET_OS_MAC` is defined and does not compile on a current macOS
  SDK without it. It changes no code path (the gzip stream only decompresses
  `.gz` font files).

## The configuration, and why it matters

`include/freetype/config/ftoption.h` is byte-identical to the one the package
installs, so the options are FreeType's defaults. Two of them decide what the
server's glyphs look like:

- **`FT_CONFIG_OPTION_SUBPIXEL_RENDERING` is off.** `FT_Library_SetLcdFilter`
  is a stub (in the package's `libfreetype.so.6.12.3` it disassembles to
  `mov w0, #7; ret`, `FT_Err_Unimplemented_Feature`), and
  `FT_RENDER_MODE_LCD` renders a greyscale glyph and repeats each coverage into
  all three subpixels (`src/smooth/ftsmooth.c:305-335`). app_server asks for
  LCD glyphs (`FontEngine.cpp:552-555`) and gets grey ones.
- **`TT_CONFIG_OPTION_SUBPIXEL_HINTING` is off**, so the TrueType bytecode
  interpreter is v35, the only one compiled in. 2.6.3 predates
  `FREETYPE_PROPERTIES`, so nothing in the environment changes that either.

The library's `ftconfig.h` is the stock ANSI one in `include/`; the package's
was generated by configure, and differs only in autoconf's `HAVE_*` macros and
in how it finds the integer sizes. FreeType's rasteriser and hinters are
integer arithmetic (its only floating point is in trace output), so the
compiler cannot change a glyph. The compile flags are FreeType's library-build
ones, `FT2_BUILD_LIBRARY` and `-O2`.

One platform caveat: on 64-bit Windows `long`, and so `FT_Long`, is 32 bits
where the server's arm64 has 64. FreeType is written to give the same results
either way, but the identity check below only runs on a 64-bit-`long` host.
The vendored library and the client's text path compile for
`x86_64-windows-gnu`, `aarch64-windows-gnu`, `x86_64-macos` and `aarch64-macos`
(checked with `zig cc`); they were not run there.

## How it is checked

- `make freetype-identity-check` (`tools/freetype_identity`) loads the image's
  own `libfreetype.so` -- a Haiku arm64 ELF that needs nothing from
  `libroot.so` but C library calls, so it loads on Linux arm64 with a stub --
  next to this copy, and compares everything app_server takes from FreeType for
  every glyph of a face at every size from 5 to 30 px: the outline after an
  unhinted, a hinted and a hinted-LCD load, the unscaled load, metrics and
  advances, the LCD, grey and mono renders, and kerning. Over the test faces and
  the guest's Noto and Charter families (9,747,712 comparisons) nothing
  differs; with this copy built with `TT_CONFIG_OPTION_SUBPIXEL_HINTING`
  instead, 62,262 of 160,496 comparisons on Noto Sans at 8-14 px do.
- `make painter-oracle-check` renders the text scenes (`tests/text_scenes.hpp`)
  through app_server's own `AGGTextRenderer`, `FontCacheEntry`, `FontEngine` and
  Painter, built on this library, and the render tests require the client to
  match every pixel.
- `test_this_build_rasterizes_with_the_canonical_images_freetype`
  (`tests/tests.cpp`) reads the version, the LCD filter stub and the
  interpreter version back from the linked library at run time.

## Updating

Only when the image's FreeType changes. Download that release, check its
sha256 against the recipe that built the image's package, copy the same file
set, take `ftmodule.h` from the package's installed headers, diff its
installed `ftoption.h` against the tarball's (and carry any difference as a
`haiku-config` override, not an edit), update this file and
`canonical_glyph_rasterizer` (`include/haiku_remote/types.hpp`), and rerun
`make painter-goldens` and `make freetype-identity-check`. No file here is
edited by hand.
